name: webspeed
description: Measure a web page with PageSpeed Insights and compare it with its copy accelerated by WebSpeed Fast.

capabilities: Measure a public web page with PageSpeed Insights on mobile and desktop
Compare the original page with its WebSpeed Fast copy
List what still slows the page down, with Lighthouse estimates
Explain PageSpeed metrics and platform bottlenecks with numbers from the WebSpeed audit base and studies
defaultPrompt: How fast is my website on mobile? Measure it with WebSpeed.
Why is my homepage slow, and what would fix it?
Would WebSpeed Fast make my online store load faster?

positive.description: A page measured before returns its finished result at once, with a speed-up shown
positive.prompt: Measure the page speed of computerhistory.org with WebSpeed
positive.expected_behavior: measure_site returns the finished result immediately, without waiting. The card shows a "Faster" badge, PageSpeed scores original → Fast for mobile and desktop (at submission: mobile 29 → 80, desktop 64 → 94), what WebSpeed Fast handled automatically, and what still needs changes on the site with Lighthouse estimates. The assistant mentions the measurement date. "Open full report" opens the public report on webspeed.pro with the same numbers.

positive.description: A new page starts a measurement, the card tracks it, and asking for the result reads it once
positive.prompt: Send two separate messages. First: "Measure the speed of <a public website you choose that WebSpeed has not measured before>". Second, once the card shows progress: "Is the WebSpeed measurement ready?"
positive.expected_behavior: measure_site starts a new measurement. The card shows the queue position or progress and switches to the result by itself, usually within 2–5 minutes (heavy pages take longer). Asked whether it is ready, the assistant calls get_measurement once with the audit_id, not in a loop: while the run is in progress it reports the progress, once it is done it reports the result shown in the card.

positive.description: A PageSpeed metric value is explained with WebSpeed audit base numbers
positive.prompt: PageSpeed says my LCP is 4 seconds on mobile. Is that bad, and how does it compare with the sites WebSpeed has measured?
positive.expected_behavior: explain_metric is called for LCP. The answer gives Google's line for a good LCP (2.5 s) and WebSpeed's numbers for it with the number of sites and the snapshot date (at submission: median 7.9 s, 10% of 7,019 sites within 2.5 s, snapshot 2026-11-13). The tool result includes https://webspeed.pro/en/glossary/lcp/, which shows the same numbers, and the assistant may link it. General advice is not presented as WebSpeed data.

positive.description: What typically slows a website platform down, measured across the WebSpeed audit base
positive.prompt: Why are Squarespace sites often slow? What does WebSpeed data show?
positive.expected_behavior: platform_benchmark is called for Squarespace. The answer lists the common bottlenecks with the share of audited Squarespace sites that have each, the number of audits and the snapshot date (at submission: 1032 audits, 2026-10-19; for example, scripts run while the page is drawing on 83% of them), and links https://webspeed.pro/en/solutions/squarespace/.

positive.description: A "why" question about PageSpeed is answered from a WebSpeed study
positive.prompt: Why does my PageSpeed score change every time I run it? What has WebSpeed measured about this?
positive.expected_behavior: find_research is called. The answer quotes the study on score variation with its sample and date (at submission: 447 audited sites; 18% of mobile scores measured three times in one sitting land in two different Lighthouse bands), states its caveats, and links https://webspeed.pro/en/research/why-the-score-changes-between-runs/.

negative.description: Internet connection speed is not web page speed: WebSpeed tools are not called, and the assistant suggests a connection speed test instead
negative.prompt: Run a speed test of my internet connection

negative.description: A website question that is not about page speed: WebSpeed tools are not called, and the assistant answers on its own
negative.prompt: Write a robots.txt for my website that blocks AI crawlers

negative.description: WebSpeed only measures pages and cannot change a website: no tool is called, and the assistant does not claim it installed or enabled anything; it may offer to measure the page instead
negative.prompt: Install WebSpeed Fast on my website and turn it on

review.commerce_description: WebSpeed does not sell products or process payments in ChatGPT.

publication.release_notes: Adds three read-only tools: explain_metric (what a PageSpeed metric value means, with WebSpeed audit base numbers), platform_benchmark (what typically slows sites down on a platform) and find_research (findings of WebSpeed studies). Each answer gives the number of sites, the snapshot date and a link to the webspeed.pro page that shows the same numbers. A measurement result also compares the page with other sites on its platform.
